set.body:
SYSTEMATIC DEFECT, found by smoke-testing the export surface. Two mirror-image cases, each of which names the exact category the user's object appears to belong to and then refuses it.

  crossnobis(geometry(plan))       object class effect_geometry,effect_form
    -> `x` must be a compiled geometry or crossnobis plan.

  rdm(plan_crossnobis(...))        object class effect_crossnobis_plan
    -> RDM requires a geometry plan or complete effect form.

In the first, the user holds an object produced by geometry() - which is literally the function that COMPILES the geometry, returning class effect_geometry - and is told the argument must be a compiled geometry. In the second, the user holds an object produced by plan_crossnobis(), named a plan and classed as a plan, and is told the argument must be a plan.

THE CAUSE IS A VOCABULARY INVERSION. The messages use 'compiled geometry' to mean effect_geometry_PLAN, while the API uses geometry() for the function that compiles and effect_geometry for its result. So the word 'compiled' points at the un-materialized object in the prose and at the materialized object in the class names. A user cannot reconcile the two, and the message gives them no way to discover which sense is meant.

CONTRAST WITH THE CASE THAT WORKS, from the same smoke test - passing a geometry PLAN to crossnobis gives an excellent message:

  crossnobis(plan_geometry(...))
    -> Crossnobis requires an explicit noise-precision metric schedule; an implicit
       Euclidean geometry has no declared noise metric.

Requirement, reason, and the actual mismatch. So the same function has one good message and one self-refuting one depending on which wrong object it receives.

RELATION TO OTHER BEADS. This generalises bd-01KZYAV952F3MJFDWR43FH8XTV, which I filed as a single instance of rdm() refusing a crossnobis plan with a contradictory message. Having now found the mirror case, the finding is not that one message is badly worded - it is that the class vocabulary used in error messages does not match the class vocabulary used in the API, and the mismatch produces contradictions wherever the two families meet. That is the same seam as bd-01KZYDTPTS6QPHCM07P1PPH396 (cross_partitions on a fit) and bd-01KZYJAQ7Y06F5C1P7KG6MAJE4 (the metric-recipe advice), now from a fourth direction.

FIX, and it is the general form of the rule proposed on bd-01KZY9B80RMYJD4QDAFS5ZBQSM: name what was RECEIVED, not only what was required.

  before  `x` must be a compiled geometry or crossnobis plan.
  after   crossnobis() needs a plan, not a materialized form; you supplied an
          <effect_geometry>. Build one with plan_crossnobis(fit, at, over, metric = ...),
          or use rdm()/contrast() to query the geometry you already have.

METHOD NOTE: this was found by calling exported functions with valid objects of the wrong kind and reading what came back - roughly thirty calls. Most refusals in that sweep were correct and well-worded. The two above were the only self-refuting ones, and neither is reachable from any vignette, which is presumably why no reviewer found them.
set.title: Error-message vocabulary is inverted relative to the API's own class names, producing self-refuting messages
